prompt: Complete a custom checked exception: InvalidAgeException must carry the offending value (exposed via getBadAge()), and validate must throw it for any age outside 0-130.
explanation: A custom exception is an ordinary class that extends Exception, so it can carry extra state -- here a final int set in the constructor and exposed through getBadAge(), giving the catcher structured data instead of just a message string. Because InvalidAgeException extends Exception (not RuntimeException) it is a CHECKED exception, which is why validate must declare it with a throws clause. The validator throws for anything outside 0-130 and simply returns for valid input; the test proves both paths by catching the exception and inspecting its payload.
hints: Give the nested exception a private final int field and assign it in the constructor right after the super(...) call.
getBadAge() just returns that field -- this is how an exception carries structured information to its catcher.
validate only acts when the age is out of range: one if testing both bounds, throwing your custom exception with the offending value. A valid age needs no code at all.
